message.content:
Reduce each base modulo \(7\):

\[
29 \equiv 1 \pmod{7}
\]

So,

\[
29^{13} \equiv 1^{13} \equiv 1 \pmod{7}
\]

Also,

\[
5 \equiv 5 \pmod{7}
\]

By Fermat’s little theorem, \(5^6 \equiv 1 \pmod{7}\), and since \(13 \equiv 1 \pmod{6}\),

\[
5^{13} \equiv 5^1 \equiv 5 \pmod{7}
\]

Thus,

\[
29^{13} - 5^{13} \equiv 1 - 5 \equiv -4 \equiv 3 \pmod{7}
\]

The answer is 3.
